observations.text:
Rain runs down the inside of Kite City’s dome. Above it, Helion’s towers stay dry. Below it, your chip lights up: “Ward Four noodle stall. Tonight. I have work.” Quill, a broker. You need the work. You have not said yes.

The year is 3055. You carry things, open doors, find what someone would rather lose. People call you a runner. Across the street, a Glass Chapel advertisement promises a night without regret: pay to edit an hour of memory. The original survives in a sliver of glass called a shard.

The stall’s amber light cuts through the rain a few streets ahead. Find Quill. Hear the offer before you decide what it is worth.

choices.text:
1
Walk toward the stall.

2
Go straight to Quill’s meeting.
Details
Skip the prologue and hear the job. No money, items, or stats change.

observations.text:
You carried parcels across the flats before you came under the dome. Out there, a bad route could kill you. In Kite City, a good route can belong to someone who charges twice. You are still a courier. You are learning the price of staying.

Your chip holds 40 creds. Helion still keeps a file under your old name. Every official job asks for a number that leads back to it. Quill’s work comes through quieter doors.

Your route book has a blank page for the next crossing. You would like to choose the destination this time. Quill brokers jobs without an official record. Tonight you are going to hear one, under the street handle Replay. What do you want it to buy?

observations.text:
You want a way beyond the next closed door. Steam rises through the awnings. A woman behind the noodle counter wipes rain off a menu while the tower advert plays above her: “Sleep without yesterday.” She sees you looking.

“Funny thing to sell,” she says. “Yesterday.”

Quill sits at the far end of her counter, coat buttoned, bowl untouched. He raises two fingers. You have a moment before you take the stool.

1
Ask her what she means.
Details

2

observations.text:
“A regular came in last winter,” she says. “He'd sold an argument with his wife to make the rent. Remembered getting paid. Didn't remember what he needed to apologize for. Asked me to write it down.”

She flattens the damp menu. “I sell dinner. But if someone hires you to carry an hour, ask whose it was before you ask what it pays.”

Quill moves his bowl aside. You still need work; now you have a question to take with you.

choices.text:

observations.text:
Quill moves his bowl aside. "Replay. Mara Voss, Helion logistics. Glass Chapel edits her memory at dawn. Bring me the original hour, intact. Fifty now, two hundred on delivery. Her bodyguard is Kerr. He is paid to stop you."

You came to buy yourself a way beyond the next closed door. One job will not do that alone. It might be a start. Somewhere above the rain, a file with your old name is still open.

The stallholder’s story stays with you. Whose hour are you being asked to carry? Quill has not touched his dinner. You have not agreed to the job.

Quill turns the untouched bowl away from the edge. "Do not give me an easy yes. I need you to come back with the hour."

"Fifty now. Two hundred when the shard is in my hand and not wandering around in your bloodstream. Kerr is her shadow. Kerr is why the number is not prettier."

He keeps his chip on his side of the counter. "The advance has to get you through the door. Ask for more if that is what the work needs."

"Ninety when you take the job. I need that extra money to get you through the door, not just get me a yes."

Ninety is already on your chip. Try not to donate it to a door. You tell Quill this job is a step toward getting out. "Start by choosing how you get in," he says.

"Three ways in. The front sells forgiveness to anyone with an appointment. The hatch behind the incinerator is for people who still sweat. The choir door runs on an old Helion pad. I would not kiss it."

The penitent pass is a hundred. It scans often enough. Glass Chapel is three streets over. You leave the steam of the stall for its white light.

Antiseptic and cheap incense are losing a fight in here. A bowl of extracted optics waits under a sign that says RECYCLE in a font meant to be kind.

No one is shouting yet. You file that under temporary.

The chair room is up a short stair. Someone is humming a hymn with the rhythm taken out.

You wanted a way beyond the next closed door. This one leads to somebody else's hour. You still have to decide what to do with it.

"You are not on the penitent list. Dawn puts Mara Voss in that chair so Helion can edit a crime out of her. The next sentence should be one you can survive."

observations.text:
"Mara Voss signed the coolant dump into Ward Nine. Three hundred people. One memo. No funeral that used their names. The shard is the only unedited hour.

Sell it to Quill and he sells it to Helion, and Helion buys the last copy of its own crime. Break it, and I leak what I remember. Memory is weaker than a shard. It is still a fire."

She waits. The optic is dark now, which means she is doing this as a person.

Lumen nods at the plinth. "Copy it. Then we both leave holding a fire. Do not get clever and die."

Mara's voice, unedited: "I signed the coolant dump. Ward Nine. Three hundred on the night shift. I want that sentence to stay in my mouth."

Mara’s recorded voice, still unedited: "Helion told me the dump was a flush, not a kill. I signed because the night shift was already in the building and I thought the tower would move them. They did not move them."

She does not ask you to forgive it. She asks you to keep the reason attached to the crime.

Sera holds the cover sheet at the edge of the table. No approved recording from Nia was obtained; the public account quotes none of her words.

Sera asks whether to file the account or withdraw it. The names are still waiting at the wall.

observations.text:
The public account is filed. Someone can question it after you leave. Sera turns from the records table to the wall: the account is there, but the names are still waiting for a voice.

She keeps her pencil in her hand. ‘We still have the names.’

choices.text:
1
Read the names you kept.
Details
You have to be carrying the truth, not just the mood.

2

Details
Lumen's fire, or the copy, is already walking.

3

observations.text:
You leave the wall to the weather. The leak you already made can live without your voice on this wall.

Sera does not chase you. Ward Nine has practice at people who get to the stair and then remember they have somewhere dry to be. The names stay. The rain stays. You stay a person who could have spoken and did not, which is its own title.

Halfway down the stair you hear Sera set the pencil against the next line. She does not ask you to turn around. Her voice reaches you through the rain.

"Mind the broken step. It's the second one down."
